source.title: On the geometry and topology of representations: the manifolds of modular addition
source.authors: Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja; G. McCracken; Harley Wiltzer; Vincent Létourneau; Colin Daniels; D. Precup; J. Love

record.tranche_reason: Compares learned modular-addition representations and circuit interpretations using PCA, phase-alignment statistics, and persistent homology, rather than testing the original grokking training-trajectory measure.
record.gate_note: The study compares learned representations across modular-addition architectures. It does not report training/test accuracy trajectories, the delay after overfitting, or how delay changes with training-set size. Weight decay is specified as a training hyperparameter but is not manipulated as a causal test. Optimizer or numerical-artifact explanations and realistic large-model settings are not tested.
record.test_reason: It asks whether modular-addition networks of different architectures converge to one algorithm, which is V6's question. It answers with a different method: first-layer PCA, phase-alignment distributions over 703 runs per architecture, MMD tests and persistent homology. It measures no training trajectories, so it bears on no other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors claim the Clock representation does not occur naturally: first-layer representations are always a vector-addition disc (pizza) or a torus. They say this resolves Zhong et al.'s counter-example and restores the universality hypothesis for modular addition.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes learned representation geometry and topology using phase statistics, PCA, MMD, and persistent homology; it does not reproduce a grokking accuracy-trajectory experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture changes the observed intermediate geometry and phase-alignment distribution. The maximum-activation and center-of-mass estimators yield similar qualitative PADs, with reported differences in their distributions.
record.problems: The study does not measure grokking or generalization accuracy over training. Its evidence for a shared algorithm is indirect: representation geometry and topology are measured rather than the complete computation being established as identical. Some results are described from figures, and the paper itself notes limitations of persistent homology for detecting small-radius holes. The analysis is restricted to modular addition.
record.rows_left_out: Not all pairwise PAD MMD comparisons in Appendix C.1, torus-distance MMD comparisons in Appendix D, and all pairwise MMD comparisons for the Zhong et al. metrics in Appendix E.2 are itemized. The included rows retain the comparisons most directly illustrating similarity and differences across architectures; omitted comparisons are additional pairwise values from those tables.

untested.parts: No accuracy trajectories, delay or training-set-size effect.
No training dynamics or progress measures.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization or norm manipulation.
Weight decay is fixed per architecture, not varied. No critical dataset size or ungrokking.

Untested: tasks other than modular addition with n=59; hyperparameter sweeps (each architecture had its own fixed learning rate and weight decay, confounded with architecture); identity of the full computation beyond representation geometry.

missing.what: Normalized post-ReLU activation sums concentrate on the a=b diagonal for MLP-Add, Pizza and Clock alike. The authors say this undercuts Zhong's defining Pizza signature.
Claim, from Theorem 4.1 plus empirical validation, that the Clock representation does not occur naturally in practice.
Numeric Betti-number percentages per layer and architecture over 100 seeds, e.g. the share of disc versus torus in layer 1.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'peer_reviewed: ICLR 2025' is not supported. The text is marked Preprint, arXiv v1 dated 31 Dec 2025. Hyperparameters (learning rate, weight decay) differ by architecture, confounding architecture effects. MMD values in the Figure 5 caption disagree with Table 1. The Appendix D models have 512 neurons, not 1024. Table interpretation labels for the Zhong metrics contradict the prose claim of closeness. Grokking dynamics are not studied at all.

versions.untested_parts: Training/test accuracy over time, delayed generalization after overfitting, and the effect of training-set size.
Gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, and continuous progress measures predicting an accuracy jump.
Grokking on non-algorithmic data and causal effects of initialization scale or weight norm.
Delayed generalization during realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Whether low-norm bias favors a more efficient circuit, critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.

Tests representation geometry and topology across modular-addition architectures and training runs, but does not establish exact identity of the full computation or convergence under a broad sweep of architectures and hyperparameters.
Adaptive-optimizer instability, floating-point softmax limits, and whether controlling them removes grokking.

relationships.condition: MLP-Add, Attention 0.0 (Pizza) and Attention 1.0 (Clock), modular addition n=59
relationships.reason: Same first-layer disc geometry (>99% variance in 2 PCs), diagonal-aligned phases across hundreds of runs, small attention-vs-attention PAD MMD, and matching Betti topology across depth (r1-r3, r5-r7, r9, r10, r16, r17).
relationships.display_finding: First-layer discs had >99% variance in two principal components, with diagonally aligned phases across hundreds of runs, small distributional differences between attention models, and matching Betti topology across depth.

relationships.condition: MLP-Concat versus the others, and MLP-Add versus attention on distributional and Zhong metrics
relationships.reason: MLP-Concat learns a torus and a different layer path; sameness is claimed only as a factorization of one map. MLP-Add and attention PADs differ significantly. Zhong metrics still separate the attention models (r4, r8, r11-r15, r18-r22).
relationships.display_finding: MLP-Concat learned a torus and a different layer trajectory, MLP-Add and attention models differed significantly in PADs, and Zhong metrics distinguished the attention models.

relation.reason: Reports original empirical comparisons and a theoretical argument bearing on algorithmic universality across modular-addition architectures.

tranche.reason: Tests V6's universality question through representation geometry, phase-distribution comparisons and persistent homology.

source_check.notes: The evidence concerns shared manifolds and factorizations, with no grokking training trajectories reported. Retain the source's Figure 5/Table 1 and Appendix E prose/table inconsistencies; Appendix D specifies 512 neurons for Figure 7 despite Appendix A.1's general 1024-neuron statement.

statements.correction: Document status: Preprint; ICLR review status: not established by supplied text; first-layer geometry: shared disc for MLP-Add, Pizza and Clock; phase alignment: diagonal concentration.
statements.problem: The geometry and alignment findings are supported, but reviewed status is not established: the supplied document is marked Preprint. The separate LayerNorm study is outside this check.
